title: Hackers Hijack 3,562 Redis Servers via Rogue Replication to Deploy XMRig Miner
content_md: Threat actors compromised 3,562 internet-exposed Redis servers in a large cryptomining campaign that abused Redis replication features to install XMRig . The attackers targeted unauthenticated instances and used rogue replication servers to write malicious cron jobs onto vulnerable Linux systems. The campaign was uncovered after researchers found an exposed attacker-controlled directory containing 147 files, including Python exploit scripts, campaign logs, portable Python runtimes, Windows registry hives, and infrastructure data. The recovered logs showed that the operators scanned 12,966 Redis hosts and successfully compromised thousands of them across two separate campaign runs. The affected systems ran Redis versions from 2.8.17 through 7.2.0. This wide version range indicates that the attacks did not rely on a newly disclosed software vulnerability. Instead, the main weakness was unsafe Redis deployment, especially instances exposed to the internet without authentication enabled. Redis Servers Hijacked The attackers used Redis’s legitimate master-replica synchronization process as an attack mechanism. Their tools first checked whether a target accepted Redis commands without authentication. They then changed the Redis working directory and database filename through CONFIG SET commands.
